newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India offers 50,000/T Dec naphtha from Bombay.
newsitem.headline: India offers 50,000/T Dec naphtha from Bombay.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) is selling by tenders 50,000 tonnes of naphtha for December lifting from Bombay on the Indian west coast, industry sources said on Thursday.

One tender is offering 25,000 tonnes of high aromatic naphtha (HAN) for December 5-7 lifting and the other 25,000 tonnes of low aromatic naphtha (LAN) is for December 10-12 lifting, both on a free-on-board (fob) basis.
Both tenders will close on November 28 and bids are valid until November 29.

In its last tender, IOC sold 30,000 tonnes of HAN lifting November 20-22 to Dutch trader Vitol at $36.63 a tonne below U.S. Gulf spot quotes on an fob basis from Cochin on the west coast, industry sources said on Wednesday.
IOC sold its last LAN cargo to Swiss trader Glencore at $28.72 a tonne below Northwest European quotes, fob Vizag on the east coast, lifting November 24-26.
